visual: Compact rounded shrub with green, cream and pink variegated foliage, yellow-bronze young growth and lightly scented white flowers.
water: Water regularly while establishing; once established, water during prolonged dry spells.
soil: Fertile, well-drained chalk, loam or sand; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged ground; young plants benefit from shelter from severe frost and cold winds.
prune: Lightly trim in late winter or early spring, removing dead or frost-damaged shoots and shortening overlong growth.
hardinessNote: Generally hardy in much of the UK once established; exposed young plants benefit from winter shelter.
resilience: Drought tolerant once established and generally low-maintenance.
uses: Borders, low hedges, containers, slopes and small gardens.
uncertain: UK sources vary between H4 and H5 for Tricolor Charm; H5 is used here because several sources report tolerance close to −15°C, although young or exposed plants may be less hardy.

visual: Large rounded shrub with bronze-flushed young leaves maturing golden yellow, then developing coral, orange and red autumn colour beneath airy flower plumes.
water: Water while establishing; established plants tolerate short dry periods.
soil: Fertile, well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sand; acid, neutral or alkaline.
prune: Little pruning is needed; remove dead or misplaced wood in late winter. Hard pruning encourages larger foliage but reduces flowering.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most UK locations, though young shoots can be affected by late frost.
resilience: Generally pest-free and tolerant of dry conditions once established.
uses: Specimen shrub, mixed borders and strong foliage contrast.

visual: Upright dogwood with dark green leaves developing rich purple to almost black tones, silvery-grey undersides and striking red winter stems.
water: Water regularly while establishing; established plants tolerate both moderately dry and moist conditions.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; best in neutral to acid conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and extreme drought.
prune: Little routine pruning is required; remove dead, damaged or badly placed stems in late winter.
hardinessNote: Very hardy across the UK; breeder information indicates tolerance well below typical UK winter temperatures.
resilience: Robust, adaptable and low-maintenance once established.
uses: Hedges, screens, winter stem displays, mixed borders and urban planting.
uncertain: RHS and breeder information centres on about 1.5 m mature height, while some trade descriptions suggest plants may eventually approach 2 m.

visual: Very vigorous self-clinging climber with glossy three-lobed leaves that turn brilliant crimson and purple in autumn, followed by dull blue berries.
water: Water while establishing; established plants usually need little supplementary watering.
soil: Fertile, well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sand; acid, neutral or alkaline.
prune: Prune in early winter to control size, with additional summer trimming around roofs, gutters and windows.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; plant contact may irritate skin.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most UK locations, including severe winters.
resilience: Very vigorous and highly adaptable once established.
uses: Large walls, facades, fences and boundary structures.

visual: Deciduous climber producing very large pale pink flowers with a prominent deeper pink central stripe, flowering in early summer and again later.
water: Keep evenly moist while growing, especially during establishment and dry summer weather.
soil: Deep, fertile, moisture-retentive but well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sand; neutral to alkaline.
soilWarning: Keep the root zone cool and shaded; avoid waterlogging and soils that dry out severely in summer.
prune: Pruning Group 2: in February remove dead or weak growth to strong buds, then lightly prune after the first flower flush if required.
toxicity: Sap may irritate skin; harmful if eaten.
hardinessNote: Fully hardy throughout the UK in suitable well-drained soil.
resilience: Cold hardy and reliable once established, though susceptible to clematis wilt and occasional insect pests.
uses: Trellises, obelisks, walls, fences and large containers.

visual: Compact evergreen ivy with shallowly lobed grey-green leaves irregularly edged and splashed with silver-grey and creamy white.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate moderate dry periods.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; tolerant of most soil types and pH levels.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging; dry soil beside walls may require extra watering while the plant establishes.
prune: Trim as required to control spread, ideally in late winter or early spring, and keep growth clear of gutters and windows.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; foliage and sap may cause skin irritation or allergic reactions.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most UK locations; exposed variegated foliage can be scorched by cold drying winds.
resilience: Tough and adaptable once established, tolerating a wide range of light conditions.
uses: Walls, ground cover, banks, containers and shady boundaries.
uncertain: The RHS cultivar profile records no flowers for 'Glacier'; some general ivy nursery descriptions mention flowering on mature adult growth, so flowers are not treated as a dependable feature here.
